cases.question: What is COMP 4537 Internet Software Architecture about?
cases.standalone_question: What is the course content and description for COMP 4537 Internet Software Architecture at BCIT?
cases.answer_excerpt:
**COMP 4537 Internet Software Architecture** is a 3-credit course focused on the design, development, and management of web APIs. It is offered as a common course in Level 4 of the full-time Computer Systems Technology (CST) Diploma program.

### Key Topics Covered
* **RESTful APIs:** Understanding what RESTful APIs are, why they matter, and how HTTP and REST APIs relate.
* **Core Operations & Constraints:** Exploring CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations, REST constraints, and the proper use of HTTP status codes.
* **Security:** Securing backend API servers and API services using HTTPonly cookies, public/private keys, JWT, SSL, oAuth, and Bearer Tokens.
* **Asynchronous Programming:** Working with NodeJS, modules, and Promises to manage asynchronous operations.
* **Microservices & Web Architecture:** Exploring microservices, API calls (AJAX, CSRF, CORS), and modern web architecture trends.

### Course Details
* **Prerequisites:** COMP 1537 and COMP 3522.
* **Format:** A 15-week course consisting of 3 hours of lectures per week (45 total hours).
* **Passing Grade:** Minimum 50%.
* **Instructor:** Amir Amintabar (aamintabar@bcit.ca).

### Sources
* https://www.bcit.ca/courses/internet-software-architecture-comp-4537/
* https://www.bcit.ca/outlines/20261088086/
* https://www.bcit.ca/programs/computer-systems-technology-diploma-full-time-5500dipma/

cases.question: What are the entrance requirements for the Computer Systems Technology diploma?
cases.standalone_question: What are the entrance requirements for the Computer Systems Technology diploma?
cases.answer_excerpt:
For the full-time Computer Systems Technology (CST) diploma, applicants must meet the program's entrance requirements, and applications are accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. 

While the specific high school course grades for the full-time program are not detailed in the available documents, the program offers a **Direct Entry** pathway to level 2 or 3 if you have completed equivalent coursework at BCIT or another institution. 

To apply for Direct Entry, you must:
* Email cstdiploma@bcit.ca to request a pre-assessment information kit.
* Submit a completed pre-entry assessment approved by the program area.
* Provide proof of meeting all entrance requirements.

**Application Deadlines for Direct Entry:**
* **July 15th** for the Fall (September) intake.
* **November 30th** for the Winter (January) intake.

*Note: If you enter the program via Direct Entry, you will not be eligible to apply for the Co-op program.*

If you are instead looking at the **Flexible Learning (Part-time) Computer Systems Diploma**, the entrance requirements are:
* Completion of the BCIT Computer Systems Certificate (CSC) program (completed or enrolled in your final term before applying). Additional courses may be required if the certificate was not completed within the last five years.
* English language proficiency: Category 2 – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent (satisfied by taking COMM 110x in the CSC).

**Sources:**
* https://www.bcit.ca/programs/computer-systems-techn

cases.question: Am I automatically enrolled in the BCITSA Health and Dental Plan, and can I opt out?
cases.standalone_question: Am I automatically enrolled in the BCITSA Health and Dental Plan, and can I opt out?
cases.answer_excerpt:
### BCITSA Health and Dental Plan Automatic Enrollment
You are automatically enrolled in the BCITSA Health and Dental Plan if you are in a program designated as full-time by BCIT that is at least 16 weeks in length. If you meet these criteria, the plan fee is automatically included in your tuition when you register. Students in ISEP or part-time (Flexible Learning) programs are not eligible for this automatic enrollment.

### BCITSA Health and Dental Plan Opt Out
Yes, you can opt out of the plan if you already have comparable extended health and dental coverage (such as through an employer, parent, or spouse). 

To opt out, you must submit your request within the strict deadline, which is **30 days from the start of your program**. This opt-out is processed once every 12 months, and requests cannot be processed after the deadline has passed.

To meet the English Language Proficiency Category 1 requirement using the International English Language Testing System (IELTS) Academic test, you must achieve an **overall score of 7.0**, with no individual band score less than 6.0. Newly admitted international students who are offered a seat in an academic program must pay a non-refundable commitment fee of **$6,000** to secure their seat and confirm acceptance. This fee is applied directly to your tuition upon registration.

cases.question: Three quick questions: is peer tutoring free, can I opt out of the BCITSA health and dental plan, and what student residences are on the Burnaby campus?
cases.standalone_question: Is BCIT peer tutoring free, can I opt out of the BCITSA health and dental plan, and what student residences are on the Burnaby campus?
cases.answer_excerpt:
### 1) BCIT Peer Tutoring Cost and Fees
Yes, peer tutoring is completely free and available to all BCIT students. 

### 2) BCITSA Health and Dental Plan Opt-Out
Yes, you can opt out of the BCITSA Student Health and Dental Plan if you already have comparable extended health and dental coverage. To do so, you must submit your opt-out request within 30 days from the start of your program. This deadline occurs once every 12 months, and opt-outs cannot be processed after this date.

### 3) BCIT Burnaby Campus Student Housing Residences
The Burnaby campus offers the following student housing options:
* **Tall Timber Student Housing:** Opened in Fall 2025, this facility offers fully self-contained Studio rooms and Connected Single rooms.
* **Legacy Townhouses:** These host 12 students each in private rooms with shared common facilities.

cases.answer_excerpt:
### Entrance Requirements for the Computer Systems Technology (CST) Diploma

To apply for the full-time Computer Systems Technology (CST) Diploma program, you must meet the following entrance requirements:

* **English Language Proficiency:** Category 2 – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent.
* **Math:** Pre-Calculus 12 (67%) or equivalent.

Please note that admission to this program is highly competitive. Meeting the minimum requirements does not guarantee admission, as applicants are selected based on academic performance. 

If you are interested in transferring credits from previous post-secondary education, you must be accepted into the program, have earned a minimum grade of 60% in the equivalent course, and have completed the course within the last five years.

Sources:

cases.question: Which English proficiency categories does BCIT use for admissions?
cases.follow_up: What TOEFL iBT score does Category 2 require?
cases.standalone_question: What TOEFL iBT score does BCIT English proficiency Category 2 require?

prior_turns.question: Which English proficiency categories does BCIT use for admissions?

cases.answer_excerpt:
To meet the Category 2 English language proficiency requirement using the TOEFL iBT, the required score depends on your test date:

*   **Prior to January 21, 2026:** You must achieve an overall score of **86**, with no section score less than **20**.
*   **As of January 21, 2026:** You must achieve an overall score of **4.5**, with minimum section scores of **3.5** in Speaking, Writing, Reading, and Listening.

The BCIT destination code for submitting these scores is 9110. Please note that for assessment tests, your results must be dated no more than two years before your program's start date.

Sources:
* https://www.bcit.ca/admission/entrance-requirements/english-language-proficiency/
